summary: Rudolf Lange was a scholar in Japanology and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1874–1881) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1887–1923).

Rudolf Meringer worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna and studied under Johannes Schmidt at Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding posts at Vienna and the University of Graz (1899–1930).
Rudolf Much specialized in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1881–1887), where he subsequently held an academic post from circa 1893 to 1934.

Rudolf Otto was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Göttingen, and under Richard von Garbe at Tübingen; his posts included Göttingen, the University of Breslau (1914–1917), and Marburg (1917–1929).

Rudolf Otto Franke specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Bonn and Göttingen under August Fick and Franz Kielhorn, later serving at Humboldt University of Berlin (1890) and the University of Königsberg (1895–1927).
Rudolf Seydel worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1853–1856) and later held a post there from circa 1860 to 1892.

Rudolf Steiner was active in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at TU Wien (~1879–1883) and the University of Rostock (~1891), and held a post at the Goethe and Schiller Archives (~1890–1896).

Rudolf Stübe was a scholar in religious studies and related fields. Between 1890 and 1894, he studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Rostock, and the University of Halle, where he earned a Ph.D. under Richard Pischel.

Rudolf Thomas Siegfried worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and at Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, later serving as Lecturer in Sanskrit at Trinity College Dublin (1858–1862).

Rudolf Thurneysen was a linguist who studied at Basel, Leipzig under Ernst Windisch, Berlin under Heinrich Zimmer, and Paris under Henri Gaidoz. He held posts at Jena, the University of Freiburg (1887–1913), and the University of Bonn (1913–1923).

Rudolf Westphal specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Johann Gildemeister at Marburg and completed his Ph.D. at Tübingen, later holding posts at Tübingen, Breslau (1857–1862), Fellin Landesschule, Goldingen Gymnasium, and Katkov Lyceum (1875–1881).

Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Heinrich Ewald at Tübinger Stift and Eugène Burnouf. He spent his academic career at the University of Tübingen, serving as Privatdozent (1845) and Extraordinarius (1848–1895).

Rudolph Rahmann studied at Missionshaus St. Gabriel and the University of Vienna under Wilhelm Schmidt and Wilhelm Koppers. He held posts at Fu Jen Catholic University, the University of San Carlos, and the University of Fribourg (1956–1960).

Rudrapatna Shamasastry was an Indologist and historian who studied at Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, University of Madras, Oriental University, and University of Calcutta. He served at Sri Chamarajendra Samskrita Maha Patashala, Oriental Research Institute Mysore, and Mysore Archaeological Department.

Ruixuan Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Chen earned a Ph.D. from Leiden University supervised by Paul Harrison, also studying under Jens-Uwe Hartmann, and holds a faculty post at Peking University.

Rulon Wells was a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Utah (~1935–1939) and Harvard University (~1939–1942), and held a long-term post at Yale University (~1945–1989).
Rune Edvin Arvid Johansson worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Lund University and the University of Ceylon, and served as a Lecturer at Lund University.

Rupert Gethin is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his degrees at the University of Manchester under Lance S. Cousins. He held posts at the University of Bristol (from 1987) and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Ruriko Sakuma is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at Nagoya University and has held posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ruth Fuller Sasaki was a Buddhist studies and Japanology practitioner and scholar. She studied at the University of Chicago and under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Sokei-an, Zuigan Goto, and Mukai Kono, later directing the First Zen Institute and Ryōsen-an.
